domain_label: Enrollment Periods, Plan Comparison & Needs Fit
purpose: How a certified agent determines which enrollment window a beneficiary is actually in, turns that person's own doctors, medications, existing coverage and cost tolerance into a documented need-driven comparison of coverage routes, and runs an enrollment conversation in which the beneficiary rather than the agent, the family or the compensation schedule makes the election.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the agent is individually licensed for the relevant lines in the client's state and holds current plan-year certifications and carrier appointments; those requirement classes themselves are owned by the certifications-and-compliant-marketing KB and are treated here only as a precondition to check

window dates, plan designs, formularies, provider networks, penalty construction and compensation schedules change every plan year and vary by state and county, so every specific in this KB is a class to be verified against the current-year official source for that client, never a fact recited from memory
this KB is educational and operational; it does not substitute for personalized insurance, medical, tax or legal advice, and the election belongs to the beneficiary

most clients are seniors and some are situationally or cognitively vulnerable, so comprehension and ethical-contact constraints are treated as design requirements of the process rather than courtesies layered on top

no dollar amounts, premium levels, penalty amounts, subsidy thresholds or commission figures are asserted anywhere; money is described as a mechanism whose current values are looked up per case and dated in the file
exclusions: the certification, licensing and carrier-appointment stack itself, the CMS marketing-rule classes, permission-to-contact and scope-of-appointment wording and retention, compliant lead generation and community presence, and audit-surviving documentation habits in general - the certifications-and-compliant-marketing KB owns all of that; this KB only checks that those artifacts exist before the enrollment work starts

renewal-compensation mechanics, the year-round service model, mid-year plan-change and provider-issue service, annual-review practice, retention and compliant referral growth - the renewal-compensation-service-and-retention KB owns those; this KB stops at a verified, documented, effective enrollment handed over
personalized plan recommendations: this KB describes how to compare, verify and document, never which plan a named person should buy
medical, clinical, pharmacological, tax or legal advice, including whether a specific treatment will be covered or whether a client should change a medication

specific premium amounts, cost-sharing amounts, penalty amounts, subsidy income thresholds, commission figures and calendar dates, all of which are plan-year and jurisdiction specific and must be looked up in the official current-year source

employer-group benefit administration, union and retiree plan administration, and marketplace subsidy determination beyond recognizing the class and routing the client to the administrator or official source
carrier-side underwriting decisions, claims adjudication, appeals representation and anything that constitutes acting as the client's legal representative
using compensation differences between product classes as a reason, stated or unstated, to prefer one option in any comparison shown to a client

competency_questions.question: Which enrollment window is this person actually in right now, what change does it allow, and when would that change take effect?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENROLLMENT_WINDOW_TAXONOMY names the window class, the change it permits and its effective-date rule, and ELIGIBILITY_PATHWAY_MAP supplies the eligibility basis and anchor dates the window hangs on, both verified against the current plan-year source

competency_questions.question: What has to be true before I am allowed to have this conversation at all, and what exactly am I telling the client I am and am not doing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERMISSION_AND_APPOINTMENT_PRECONDITION gives the readiness gate on permission, scope, licensure and appointment, and EDUCATIONAL_ROLE_BOUNDARY gives the spoken role-and-limited-carrier disclosure and the referral map for questions outside scope

competency_questions.question: What must I know about this person before any plan name is spoken, and how do I capture it so a later recommendation is defensible as need-driven?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEEDS_INTAKE_DOSSIER lists the fact classes gathered and the written artifact they produce, including the must-keep ranking recorded in the client's own words

competency_questions.question: What coverage does this person already hold, what happens to it if they enroll, and where is the gap that creates a late-enrollment charge?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CURRENT_COVERAGE_AUDIT classifies the existing coverage and states who confirms in writing whether it can be kept, dropped or resumed, and CREDITABLE_COVERAGE_AND_LATE_PENALTY_CLASS describes the surcharge mechanism and the evidence the client must keep

competency_questions.question: How do I find out whether this client qualifies for assistance that changes both what they should buy and which windows they have, without prejudging them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DUAL_ELIGIBLE_AND_ASSISTANCE_SCREENING names the assistance classes to screen for, the respectful way to ask, and the official application paths the client is routed to

competency_questions.question: How do the two main coverage architectures actually work, and which parts of that choice are hard to undo later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVERAGE_ROUTE_ARCHITECTURE explains both routes as payment, access and cost-shape mechanisms without ranking them, and SUPPLEMENT_UNDERWRITING_WINDOW_CLASS states the guaranteed-acceptance window asymmetry and the state-variation warning

competency_questions.question: How do I check this client's own doctors and prescriptions against a candidate plan without turning a directory entry into a promise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVIDER_NETWORK_VERIFICATION specifies the two-source check, the dated record and the language that keeps it a check rather than a guarantee, and DRUG_LIST_FIT_ANALYSIS specifies the per-drug tier and utilization-management review plus pharmacy status

competency_questions.question: How do I show what a plan will really cost this person over a year without inventing numbers or reducing it to the lowest premium?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOTAL_COST_EXPOSURE_MODEL separates fixed cost, expected cost-sharing, drug-phase cost and worst-case ceiling, sources every figure to a dated current-year lookup, and presents ranges with the driving assumption named

competency_questions.question: How do I keep the shortlist honestly driven by this client's needs when the options do not all pay me the same?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEED_DRIVEN_COMPARISON_SET states the assembly rules including the do-nothing baseline and the named-gap rule, and COMPENSATION_NEUTRALITY_CONTROL states the criteria-first sequence, the written rationale and the book-skew self-audit

competency_questions.question: How do I run the meeting so the beneficiary genuinely makes the decision, including when a family member is pushing or the client is struggling to follow?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANT_ENROLLMENT_CONVERSATION gives the order of the meeting and the comprehension check, and VULNERABLE_CONSUMER_CARE gives the pacing, representative, stop and no-pressure rules

competency_questions.question: What has to be right at submission, and how do I confirm the person is actually covered on the date they think they are?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENROLLMENT_APPLICATION_EXECUTION covers window-code selection, identifier accuracy, required consent artifacts and effective-date confirmation, and POST_SUBMISSION_VERIFICATION covers acceptance, card, prior-coverage and first-fill checks with an escalation path

competency_questions.question: What file must exist afterward so a third party could reconstruct this enrollment a year later, and what is handed to the service side?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ARTIFACT_AND_DOCUMENTATION_PACK enumerates the retained artifacts and the client's own copy, and HANDOFF_TO_SERVICE_YEAR states the exit criteria and the packet the service practice receives

competency_questions.question: What do I do when the calendar has already gone wrong - a missed window, a weak special-window claim, or an election that produced the wrong result?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WINDOW_MISS_AND_REMEDY_PATHS maps the remedy classes and their consequences, routes to the program's own exception process and the neutral counseling program, and states the prohibition on manufacturing or coaching a qualifying event

competency_questions.question: How do I get through the annual window without letting volume degrade the quality of any single enrollment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONAL_CAPACITY_PLANNING gives the load forecast, the pre-season work that leaves the peak, the daily appointment ceiling and the stated cut-off that pushes work to the next slot instead of compressing a meeting

glossary.definition: A named category of period during which a beneficiary is permitted to make a specific kind of coverage election; each class differs in who qualifies, what change is allowed and when the resulting coverage begins, and each is verified per case against the current plan-year source rather than recalled.

The window class that opens around a person's first eligibility and is anchored to their eligibility event rather than to the calendar; it is the one time most beneficiaries can enter any route with the fewest conditions attached.

The recurring fall window in which most beneficiaries may change plans for the following coverage year; it concentrates the year's plan-change work into a few weeks and drives the seasonal capacity problem.

A window class opened by a documented qualifying event - moving out of a service area, losing employer or other creditable coverage, a plan contract change, a change in assistance status - whose qualification must be evidenced, never assumed or coached.

Prior coverage that the rules treat as good enough to avoid a late-enrollment charge for the relevant program part; whether a given plan counts is determined by the plan's own notice and the current rules, not by the agent's judgment.

A limited period or triggering situation in which a supplement carrier must issue a policy without medical underwriting; outside it, most states allow underwriting, which is what makes leaving the supplement route a decision that may not be reversible.

The list that says whether a plan covers a drug, at what cost tier, and under what conditions - prior authorization, step therapy or quantity limits - all of which are set per plan and per year and must be checked against the client's actual prescriptions.

An annual ceiling on a member's cost-sharing that exists in some coverage architectures and not in others; its presence or absence is the single clearest way to describe worst-case exposure without quoting a number.
The client's current arrangement carried into the comparison as an explicit option, so that changing plans has to earn its place against staying put rather than being assumed.

A provider, facility or medication the client has stated they will not give up, recorded in writing at intake and ranked before any plan is named, so that a later failure to satisfy it is visible rather than quietly traded away.

nodes.definition: Before a single needs question is asked, settle whether this contact may happen and whether this agent can actually transact for this person: the beneficiary's permission-to-contact record covers the channel being used, a scope-of-appointment-class artifact exists for the product lines about to be discussed and has satisfied its timing rule, the agent's license is active for the client's state and lines, and the current plan-year certifications and carrier appointments cover every plan that could plausibly come up in the comparison. This node owns only the yes/no readiness answer that sits at the top of the enrollment file and the rule that an unready agent reschedules rather than improvises; the wording, timing, retention and audit form of those artifacts belong to the certifications-and-compliant-marketing KB. Readiness is checked per carrier and per state, not once per season, because an agent can be fully certified and still unappointed for the one plan a client asks about.

included: the pre-meeting readiness check covering permission, scope artifact, state licensure and per-carrier appointment
the reschedule-instead-of-proceed rule and the script for it
recording the readiness result at the top of the enrollment file
excluded: the regulatory wording, timing rules and retention periods of the permission and scope artifacts, which the certifications-and-marketing KB owns
how leads that produced the contact were generated
annual recertification cadence and carrier contracting mechanics

pros.claim: Catching an appointment or licensure gap before the meeting prevents an application that cannot be submitted for the plan the client chose
pros.example: discovering during the readiness check that the carrier whose network holds the client's cardiologist is one the agent is not appointed for, and saying so at the start instead of after a two-hour comparison

pros.claim: A written readiness result gives the file a defensible first page when the enrollment is reviewed later
pros.example: a reviewer opening the file and seeing the scope artifact reference and appointment status dated before the meeting rather than reconstructed afterward

cons.claim: The gate can cost a live opportunity when a client is ready to talk and the paperwork is not yet in place
cons.example: a walk-in during the annual window who has to be booked for a later day because the scope artifact for the product line has not aged as required

cons.claim: Per-carrier checking is tedious and tempts agents into a once-per-season assumption that goes stale mid-year
cons.example: assuming a carrier appointment carried over when the carrier added a mid-year condition the agent never completed

failure_modes: starting a needs conversation on a channel the client never gave permission for
discussing a product line outside the agreed scope because the client raised it
comparing a plan the agent is not appointed to sell and then steering the client away from it to hide the gap
treating a season-opening certification sweep as proof of readiness for every carrier all year
acceptance_tests: the file records, dated before the meeting, that permission covers the channel used, a scope artifact covers the lines discussed, the license is active in the client's state, and each carrier whose plans may be shown is one the agent is appointed for
any readiness gap is recorded together with what was done about it - reschedule, restricted scope, or referral out
revisit_triggers: a carrier adds or changes an appointment or certification condition mid-year
the client asks to discuss a product line outside the agreed scope
the client moves to another state or the meeting channel changes

base.update_signal: a change in marketing-rule requirements for permission or scope artifacts, or a carrier changing its appointment and certification conditions for the plan year

nodes.definition: Say out loud, at the start and again whenever the conversation drifts, what the agent is doing and what the agent is not doing. The agent explains how coverage routes work, checks the client's own doctors and prescriptions against current-year plan sources, lays out trade-offs in both directions and writes down what was shown. The agent does not predict the client's future health, does not give medical, tax or legal advice, does not decide for the client, and discloses plainly that they represent a limited set of carriers rather than every plan available in the area. This is a working boundary, not a slogan: it determines how the inevitable 'just tell me which one you would pick' is answered, what a comparison sheet is allowed to claim, and where the conversation is routed outward - to the plan's own coverage documents, to the prescriber or pharmacist, to the official program source, or to the state health insurance counseling program that has no product to sell.

included: the spoken opening that names the agent's role, the limited-carrier disclosure and who makes the election
the answer pattern for the pick-one-for-me question that returns to the client's own recorded criteria
the outward referral map for questions past the boundary
excluded: the regulatory form and timing of required disclosures, owned by the certifications-and-marketing KB
clinical judgment about the client's care or medications
household financial, tax or estate planning

pros.claim: Stating the boundary in minute one turns a later refusal to choose for the client into a kept promise rather than an evasion
pros.example: a client who was told at the start that the decision is theirs accepts a two-sided trade-off summary at the end instead of pressing for a directive

pros.claim: A named referral map keeps the agent useful at the edge of scope instead of improvising an answer that is not theirs to give
pros.example: routing 'will my knee replacement be covered' to the plan's coverage documents and the carrier's coverage-determination process rather than guessing

cons.claim: Clients often experience the boundary as unhelpfulness and some will go to whoever sounds more certain
cons.example: a client leaving for an agent who says 'this is the best plan, sign here' and only discovering the network problem in March

cons.claim: Holding the line lengthens meetings, which collides directly with annual-window capacity
cons.example: spending twenty minutes explaining that the agent cannot promise a specific surgery is covered, during the busiest week of the year

failure_modes: sliding from explaining trade-offs into telling the client what to buy because it saves time
answering a coverage question definitively when only the plan document can answer it
omitting the limited-carrier disclosure so the client believes they have seen the whole market
letting an educational frame become a shield for saying nothing useful at all
acceptance_tests: the opening disclosure - role, limited-carrier fact, and who makes the election - is recorded in the file for every enrollment contact
every out-of-scope question in the notes has a recorded destination: plan document, prescriber or pharmacist, official program source, or counseling program
revisit_triggers: a client says they understood the agent to be recommending or choosing for them
the agent's carrier lineup changes, altering what the limited-carrier disclosure must say
a complaint or review names the advice boundary

base.update_signal: a regulator, carrier or complaint record clarifies where education ends and personalized recommendation begins for agents in this channel

nodes.definition: Treat the fact that this book is mostly seniors, some of them cognitively or situationally vulnerable, as a constraint on how the whole process is built rather than as a bedside manner. Concretely: pace the meeting to the client rather than the calendar, check comprehension by asking the client to state the trade-off back in their own words, establish early whether a spouse, adult child or power-of-attorney-class representative is present and in what role, and record that. Impose rules on the agent's own behaviour - no urgency the agent manufactured, no fear framing about what could happen if they do not act today, no exploiting a deadline that does not actually apply to this client, no election taken while the client is distressed or unwell. Recognize the signs that a client cannot presently make the decision and stop the meeting rather than proceeding with a signature, and refuse to take an election a family member wants and the beneficiary has not chosen.

included: pacing, plain-language rewording and the restate-it-back comprehension check
identifying and documenting an authorized representative's role and authority
the agent's self-imposed no-pressure rules and the stop-the-meeting criteria
excluded: clinical assessment of capacity, which the agent is not qualified to make
legal determination of guardianship or authority, which is routed to the family's own counsel
the regulatory text of prohibited marketing practices, owned by the certifications-and-marketing KB

pros.claim: A comprehension check catches misunderstandings before they become an election the client would not have made
pros.example: asking a client to explain in their own words what happens if they use a doctor outside the network, and discovering they thought the plan would still pay the same

pros.claim: Documenting who else was in the room protects both the beneficiary and the agent when a relative later disputes the enrollment
pros.example: a note that the daughter attended by speakerphone at the client's request and that the client answered every election question herself

cons.claim: Slower, stop-if-in-doubt meetings reduce how many enrollments an agent can complete in the peak weeks
cons.example: rescheduling a confused client into January-adjacent capacity that is already scarce during the annual window

cons.claim: Judging whether a client can decide today is a judgment the agent is not trained to make and can be wrong in both directions
cons.example: reading a hard-of-hearing client's slow responses as confusion and delaying a decision they were perfectly able to make

failure_modes: accepting a nodding client as an understanding client
letting a dominant relative answer the questions the beneficiary must answer
using the closing window as emotional leverage rather than as information
taking an election from a client who is clearly unwell or distressed because rescheduling is inconvenient
acceptance_tests: the file records that the client restated the central trade-off in their own words before any election was taken
where anyone other than the beneficiary participated, the file names them, their role and that the beneficiary answered the election questions
no note anywhere in the file cites a deadline or consequence that the agent cannot source to the client's actual window or plan documents
revisit_triggers: the client or a family member later says they did not understand what was chosen
a client shows a change in comprehension between contacts
guidance on protecting vulnerable consumers in this channel is updated

base.update_signal: updated guidance on vulnerable-consumer protection, or a pattern of post-enrollment confusion in the agent's own book

nodes.definition: Establish how this specific person becomes eligible and what dates follow from it, because the pathway - reaching the qualifying age, qualifying through a long-term disability determination class, or qualifying under a specific-condition class - decides which windows open, when they open, and what the person must actively file versus what happens automatically. The work is: confirm the basis from the client's own records rather than their recollection, capture the anchor dates that everything else keys off (entitlement start, birthday month, the month active employment or employer coverage ends), determine whether enrollment in the base program parts is automatic for this person or must be filed with the administering agency and by when, and record the county and permanent residence because plan availability is geographic and a county line can change the entire option set. Anything uncertain is verified against the official source or the client's own award or enrollment documents before it is used.

included: identifying the eligibility basis class and evidencing it from the client's documents
capturing anchor dates and whether base-program enrollment is automatic or must be filed
recording county and permanent residence as the geographic key to plan availability
excluded: adjudicating eligibility, which only the administering agency does
advising on when to claim retirement benefits or how that interacts with taxes
the plan comparison itself

pros.claim: Anchoring on documents rather than recollection prevents a whole comparison keyed to the wrong month
pros.example: a client sure their coverage starts the month of their birthday when their own award letter shows a different entitlement month

pros.claim: Capturing county early prevents building an option set that does not exist at the client's address
pros.example: a client living just across a county line from the town they name, where the available plan set differs from the one the agent assumed

cons.claim: Clients often cannot find the documents, so the step stalls at the moment enthusiasm is highest
cons.example: an age-in client who cannot locate their program card and must request information before the comparison can proceed

cons.claim: Non-standard pathways carry rules the agent may not have seen recently and cannot safely reconstruct from memory
cons.example: a client who qualified years earlier through a disability determination and is now aging into a different rule set

failure_modes: assuming an age-based pathway for someone who qualified another way
reading the anchor date off the client's memory rather than their card or award letter
missing that a base-program part still has to be actively filed for this person
using a mailing address that differs from the permanent residence that governs plan availability
acceptance_tests: the eligibility basis, anchor dates and county in the file each cite the document or official source they came from, with the date checked
whether base-program enrollment is automatic or must be filed for this person is recorded with the filing deadline where one applies
revisit_triggers: the client's employment, residence or disability status changes
the client produces a document that contradicts the recorded anchor date

base.update_signal: the client's own documents or the administering agency contradict the recorded eligibility basis or anchor dates

nodes.definition: Hold the enrollment-period system as a small set of window classes and, for each, the three things that actually matter in a client conversation: who qualifies, what change it permits, and when the resulting coverage takes effect. The classes are the initial window opening around first eligibility; the recurring annual election window in which most changes for the following coverage year are made; the additional open-enrollment window class available to someone already enrolled in an advantage-class plan, which permits a narrower set of changes; the general-enrollment window class for people who did not enrol when first eligible, which carries its own effective-date and surcharge consequences; and the special window classes opened by documented qualifying events such as a permanent move out of a service area, loss of employer or other creditable coverage, a plan contract or service-area change, or a change in assistance-program status. The taxonomy is also the business's demand calendar: it explains why the year has one enormous peak and a steady trickle of age-in and event-driven work around it. Dates, qualification detail and effective-date rules are verified for the current plan year per case, never quoted from last year's memory.

included: the window classes and the qualify / permitted-change / effective-date triple for each
matching a specific client's situation to exactly one window class and evidencing the match
the demand-calendar consequence: annual peak plus year-round age-in and event work
excluded: asserting current-year calendar dates, which are looked up per plan year
the remedy work when no window applies, which the remedy-paths node owns
renewal and annual-review service, owned by the renewal-service KB

pros.claim: Matching a client to exactly one window class turns a vague 'can I switch' into a concrete answer with an effective date
pros.example: telling a client who just moved permanently that a special window class applies from the move, and what evidence of the move the carrier will want

pros.claim: Knowing the effective-date rule per window prevents the most common client shock, which is a gap between signing and being covered
pros.example: an election made in one window taking effect the following month while the client assumed it started immediately

cons.claim: The class boundaries are genuinely intricate and a confident wrong answer is worse than a checked one
cons.example: treating a change of address within the same service area as a qualifying move when it may not open any window

cons.claim: Concentrating most permitted change into one annual window creates a demand peak that stresses every quality control in the process
cons.example: a book where nearly all plan changes must be discussed, verified and submitted inside a few weeks

failure_modes: telling a client they can change plans whenever they like
reusing last plan year's dates or rules without re-verification
claiming a special window on an event class that does not actually qualify
confusing the window in which an election is made with the date coverage begins
acceptance_tests: the file names the window class relied on, the evidence that the client qualifies for it, the change it permits, and the effective date it produces
every window date or rule used in the conversation cites a current plan-year source with the date it was checked
revisit_triggers: the plan year turns over or the program publishes updated window rules
the client's circumstances change in a way that could open or close a window
a carrier or the program disputes the window code used on a submitted application

base.update_signal: the program publishes plan-year window rules or dates that differ from the ones the agent has been using

nodes.definition: Run a structured intake that produces, in writing and before any plan is named, the facts the entire comparison will be built on: the medication list exactly as the client takes it including strength and quantity rather than as they remember the brand; the doctors, specialists and hospitals they intend to keep, each marked must-keep or nice-to-keep in the client's own words; chronic conditions only so far as they predict utilization, never as clinical assessment; travel patterns, snowbird arrangements and second residences; whether they are willing to accept referral and prior-authorization steps in exchange for lower fixed cost; budget tolerance expressed both as a comfortable monthly amount and as the worst month they could absorb; and any other coverage or assistance already held. The dossier is signed off verbally with the client - read back and corrected - because it is the artifact that later makes a recommendation defensible as need-driven rather than product-driven.

included: the medication list with strengths and quantities as actually taken
the provider list with a must-keep versus nice-to-keep ranking recorded in the client's words
utilization, travel, tolerance for referral steps and two-sided budget tolerance
the read-back that confirms the dossier before comparison begins
excluded: clinical interpretation of conditions or medications
verification against plan sources, which the network and formulary nodes own
any discussion of specific plans, which comes only after the dossier is fixed

pros.claim: Fixing must-keep constraints in writing before plans are named makes later steering visible and prevents constraint drift
pros.example: a client who said in week one that their oncologist is non-negotiable, so an otherwise attractive plan that excludes that practice is shown as failing rather than quietly dropped from view

pros.claim: Exact strengths and quantities are what make the drug analysis meaningful at all
pros.example: the same medication at a different strength landing on a different tier and changing which option is cheapest across the year

cons.claim: A thorough intake is long and can exhaust an older client before the comparison even starts
cons.example: forty minutes of prescriptions and providers leaving no attention left for the trade-off discussion, forcing a second meeting

cons.claim: Clients under-report - occasional drugs, a specialist they see yearly, a spouse's plan - and the gap surfaces only after enrollment
cons.example: a quarterly injection never mentioned because the client does not think of it as a prescription

failure_modes: naming a plan before the dossier exists, which anchors everything that follows
recording drug names without strength, quantity or how often they are actually taken
not distinguishing must-keep from nice-to-keep, so every provider becomes negotiable under pressure
letting a family member supply the answers about the beneficiary's own care
acceptance_tests: the dossier exists in the file, is dated before any plan was named, and was read back to the client and corrected
each provider carries a must-keep or nice-to-keep marking and each medication carries strength and quantity as taken
revisit_triggers: the client reports a new prescription, a new specialist or a change of pharmacy
a verification step contradicts something the dossier records
more than one plan year has passed since the dossier was refreshed

base.update_signal: post-enrollment problems trace back to a fact class the intake never asked about

nodes.definition: Establish exactly what coverage the person holds today and what happens to each piece if they enrol, because the most expensive mistakes in this business are made by dropping something that cannot be recovered. The classes to identify and treat differently are active employer coverage through the client's or a spouse's job, retiree or union coverage from a former employer, continuation coverage, individual marketplace coverage, veterans' and military-retiree coverage classes, employer-sponsored drug coverage, and any existing supplement or advantage-class enrollment. For each, the agent records who administers it, whether enrolling elsewhere terminates it automatically or requires an affirmative action, whether the client's spouse or dependants ride on it, and whether it can be resumed if dropped - then routes the client to the administrator or plan for the answer in writing rather than supplying it themselves. The output is a written map of current coverage with an explicit note against anything the agent could not verify.

included: classifying every current coverage the client holds and who administers it
whether enrolling elsewhere ends it automatically, whether dependants ride on it, and whether it can be resumed
routing the keep-or-drop question to the administrator and recording the answer's source
excluded: administering or interpreting employer, union or veterans' benefit rules, which belong to those administrators
telling the client to drop coverage, which is never the agent's call
marketplace subsidy determination

pros.claim: Identifying coverage that cannot be resumed converts an ordinary sale into a decision the client makes with the irreversibility in front of them
pros.example: a retiree plan that ends permanently for both spouses if the client enrols elsewhere, discovered before the election rather than after

pros.claim: Routing keep-or-drop to the administrator in writing protects the client from a guess and the agent from being the source of a costly instruction
pros.example: asking the client to obtain the employer benefits office's written statement on whether their drug coverage counts as creditable

cons.claim: Administrators are slow to answer and the client's window may close while waiting
cons.example: a benefits office that takes weeks to respond while a special window driven by a coverage-loss date runs down

cons.claim: Clients frequently misdescribe what they have, so the audit is only as good as the documents they can actually produce
cons.example: a client describing a retiree wrap plan as a supplement policy, which changes the entire analysis

failure_modes: advising a client to drop employer or retiree coverage on the agent's own reading of it
missing that a spouse or dependant rides on the coverage being dropped
assuming coverage is creditable because it looks comprehensive
treating an existing advantage-class enrollment as automatically replaceable without checking what the new election disenrolls
acceptance_tests: every current coverage is listed with its administrator, its termination behaviour on enrolling elsewhere, whether dependants ride on it, and whether it can be resumed
any keep-or-drop question is recorded as answered by the administrator or plan in writing, or flagged as unverified with the client told so before electing
revisit_triggers: employment, retirement or a spouse's coverage changes
the administrator's answer contradicts what the client reported
a plan sends notice that the existing coverage is changing or ending

base.update_signal: an administrator's written answer or a plan notice contradicts the recorded behaviour of the client's existing coverage

nodes.definition: Handle the family of rules that charges people for gaps. Three things must be true in the file: whether the coverage the client has held counts as creditable for the relevant program part, which is determined by the plan's own creditable-coverage notice and the current rules rather than by how good the coverage looks; how the late-enrollment charge class is constructed as a mechanism - a surcharge derived from the number of uncovered months, attached to premium and lasting for the period the rules specify - stated as a mechanism with the current-year construction and amounts verified per case in the official source; and what documentary evidence the client must keep and be able to produce, namely the plan's creditable-coverage notices and the employment or coverage records that establish the covered months. The deliverable is a plain-language written statement of this client's exposure, the evidence supporting it, and what they should keep in a folder for the rest of their life.

included: identifying whether prior coverage is creditable and by whose determination
explaining the surcharge as a mechanism and where its current-year values are looked up
the evidence pack the client must retain and produce
excluded: quoting penalty amounts, rates or thresholds, which are looked up per case in the official source
determining creditable status on the agent's own judgment
appealing a charge on the client's behalf

pros.claim: Framing the charge as a months-based mechanism lets a client reason about their own situation instead of fearing a number
pros.example: walking a client through counting their own uncovered months from their employment record rather than telling them what they will owe

pros.claim: Building the evidence pack early is what defends the client years later when the charge is questioned
pros.example: a client who kept every creditable-coverage notice being able to document continuous coverage during a review

cons.claim: The rules and their arithmetic change and are easy to state slightly wrong, which is itself a compliance risk
cons.example: explaining the surcharge with last plan year's construction and leaving the client with a wrong expectation

cons.claim: Raising the penalty topic frightens clients and can be mistaken for the fear-selling the ethical rules prohibit
cons.example: a client hearing a factual explanation of gap consequences as pressure to buy today

failure_modes: declaring coverage creditable without the plan's notice
quoting a penalty figure from memory or from a prior plan year
using the penalty as a closing lever rather than as a fact the client needs
letting the client discard the notices that prove their covered months
acceptance_tests: the file states whether each prior coverage is creditable and cites the plan notice or official source that determined it
the client has been given, in writing, the list of documents to retain and the mechanism by which any charge would be constructed, with no invented amounts
revisit_triggers: the program publishes a changed penalty construction for the plan year
the client produces coverage records that change the count of uncovered months

base.update_signal: the official source publishes a changed construction, duration or determination process for the late-enrollment charge class

nodes.definition: Screen every client for the assistance classes that change both what they should buy and which windows they have, and do it before the candidate set narrows rather than after an enrollment is in place. The classes are the low-income drug-subsidy class, state Medicaid-class eligibility including partial-benefit categories, the savings-program classes that pay program premium or cost-sharing, state pharmaceutical assistance programs, and manufacturer or foundation assistance tied to a specific drug. Screening means asking about income and asset ranges in a plain, non-judgmental way, explaining why it is being asked, and routing the client to the official application path - the administering agency, the state programme, or the neutral counseling programme - rather than pre-judging eligibility or filling in an application the agent is not the right party to file. Ethically this comes early because an unscreened client can be enrolled into and quietly pay for coverage that assistance would have reshaped, and because assistance status can itself open a window class.

included: the assistance classes to screen for and the plain wording that asks without shaming
routing to the official application path and recording that the referral happened
recognizing that assistance status can change plan fit and can open a window class
excluded: determining eligibility or quoting income and asset thresholds, which belong to the administering agency and change by year and state
completing the client's assistance application on their behalf where that is not the agent's role
plan-specific benefit design for assistance-eligible clients beyond identifying the class

pros.claim: Screening first prevents the quiet harm of a client paying for something assistance would have covered or reshaped
pros.example: a client on a fixed income enrolled into full-cost drug coverage who was within reach of the subsidy class and never asked

pros.claim: Assistance status can itself open a window, turning a stuck client into one with real options
pros.example: a client whose newly granted assistance status changes what changes they are permitted to make and when

cons.claim: Income and asset questions feel intrusive to proud clients and can end a conversation if asked badly
cons.example: a client who came in about a plan and hears the income question as a means test being applied to them personally

cons.claim: Screening leads to routing work the agent is not compensated for and that competes with peak-season capacity
cons.example: spending a meeting helping a client understand where to apply for assistance instead of completing an enrollment

failure_modes: skipping the screen because the client 'looks fine'
quoting eligibility thresholds instead of routing to the official determination
discouraging a client from applying because the agent assumes they will not qualify
discovering assistance eligibility only after an enrollment is already in force
acceptance_tests: the file records that the assistance screen was offered and either the client's response or their decline, dated before the comparison narrowed
any client who may qualify has a recorded referral to the official application path, with no threshold figures asserted by the agent
revisit_triggers: the client's income, household or assistance status changes
a state or federal assistance programme changes its structure for the plan year
a client reports drug costs that seem inconsistent with their screened status

base.update_signal: an assistance programme changes its structure, or the agent's own book shows clients who qualified and were never screened

nodes.definition: For every must-keep provider and facility on the intake list, check participation in each candidate plan for the coverage year the client will actually be in, using the plan's own current-year directory plus at least one independent confirmation such as the provider's office or the carrier's service line, because directories are known to carry errors and participation can differ between plan lines from the same carrier and between the individual clinician and the facility they practise at. Record what was checked, on what date, from which source, and by whom. Tell the client in plain words that participation can change during the year, that a directory entry is a check and not a guarantee, and that only the plan and the provider can confirm. For the original-plus-supplement route the question is different in kind - whether the provider participates in the base program rather than in a private network - and must be explained as a different question, not translated into network language.

included: per-provider, per-plan, per-coverage-year participation checks from two independent sources
the dated verification record and the not-a-guarantee language given to the client
distinguishing base-program participation from private-network participation
excluded: guaranteeing continued participation, which no agent can do
negotiating with providers or carriers about participation
clinical advice about changing providers

pros.claim: A two-source check catches the directory errors that otherwise surface as a January crisis
pros.example: a directory listing a specialist who the office confirms has not accepted that plan line since the prior year

pros.claim: Explicit not-a-guarantee language keeps a mid-year network change from becoming an accusation that the agent promised something
pros.example: a client whose file shows the dated check and the caveat, when the practice leaves the network in spring

cons.claim: Verification is slow, and during the annual window the confirmation calls are exactly the work that gets skipped
cons.example: three specialists to confirm for one client while four more appointments wait

cons.claim: Provider offices themselves give inconsistent answers, so the second source is not always decisive
cons.example: front-desk staff saying they take the carrier while the specific plan line is not accepted

failure_modes: treating a directory entry as a promise
checking the carrier rather than the specific plan line
verifying against the current coverage year when the client's election takes effect in the next one
checking the facility and assuming the clinician follows, or the reverse
acceptance_tests: each must-keep provider has a dated verification record naming both sources, the plan line and the coverage year checked
the file records that the client was told a directory check is not a guarantee and that participation can change during the year
revisit_triggers: the carrier publishes a directory update or a network change notice
the client adds or changes a must-keep provider
the coverage year turns over between the check and the effective date

base.update_signal: a pattern of directory entries contradicted by provider offices, or a carrier network change notice for the coverage year

nodes.definition: Test each candidate drug-coverage option against the client's actual medication list using the formulary for the coverage year the election will take effect in: whether each drug appears at all, on which cost tier, and under which utilization-management class - prior authorization, step therapy, quantity limit - plus whether the client's preferred pharmacy is in the plan's network and at what pricing status, and whether mail order changes the picture for maintenance medications. Explain the cost-phase mechanism honestly: drug cost changes as spending accumulates through the year across defined stages, so the cheapest plan in January is not necessarily the cheapest across twelve months. Model that with current-year figures pulled from the official comparison tool for this client's exact list rather than from the agent's recollection. The deliverable is a per-drug fit table with a flag on anything needing a prescriber action, a plan exception request, or a pharmacy change, and a plain statement of which drug is driving the difference between options.

included: per-drug listing, tier and utilization-management review for the correct coverage year
pharmacy network and pricing status including mail order for maintenance drugs
the cost-phase mechanism explained and modelled from the official current-year tool
excluded: advising the client to change or stop a medication, which belongs to the prescriber and pharmacist
quoting drug prices or thresholds from memory
filing the coverage-determination or exception request as if the agent were the prescriber

pros.claim: Running the client's real list through the official tool exposes differences that no summary brochure shows
pros.example: two plans with similar headline drug coverage separating sharply once one specialty medication's tier and restriction are applied

pros.claim: Flagging a restriction before enrollment gives the client and prescriber time to act instead of discovering it at the pharmacy counter
pros.example: spotting that a maintenance drug needs prior authorization and telling the client to raise it with the prescriber before the effective date

cons.claim: Formularies change between the comparison and the coverage year, so a good analysis can still be overtaken
cons.example: a drug moving tier or gaining a restriction in the new plan year after the client has already elected

cons.claim: The analysis is only as good as the medication list, and clients routinely omit occasional or seasonal drugs
cons.example: an as-needed inhaler left off the list that turns out to be the most expensive item under the chosen plan

failure_modes: checking coverage of a drug but not its tier or restrictions
using the current coverage year's formulary for an election that takes effect in the next one
ignoring pharmacy network status so the modelled cost never matches reality
presenting the January cost as the year's cost and hiding the phase mechanism
acceptance_tests: every medication on the dossier appears in the fit table with listing status, tier, restrictions, and the coverage year checked
the pharmacy used in the model is the client's own and its network status is recorded, and the cost figures cite the official tool and the date run
revisit_triggers: the client starts, stops or changes a medication or pharmacy
the plan publishes a formulary change for the coverage year
a first fill after the effective date costs materially more than modelled

base.update_signal: a published formulary change for the coverage year, or first-fill costs that diverge from the modelled figures

nodes.definition: Explain the two dominant architectures as mechanisms rather than as brands or verdicts. In the original-program-plus-supplement route the base program pays first, a standardized supplement policy covers defined portions of what the program leaves, drug coverage is purchased separately, provider access follows program participation rather than a private network so portability across the country is high, and cost sits mostly in predictable monthly premium whose rating behaviour over time varies by state. In the advantage-class route a private plan administers the benefits under contract, cost shifts away from fixed premium toward per-service cost-sharing that is bounded by an annual out-of-pocket maximum, access runs through a network with referral and prior-authorization steps, drug coverage is usually bundled, and additional benefit classes may be included. The comparison is drawn on the axes a client actually lives with - predictability versus lower fixed cost, freedom of access versus coordinated care, portability versus local depth, simplicity versus paperwork - and never as better or worse, because which axis matters is the client's judgment and not the agent's.

included: how each route pays, grants access and shapes cost, described as mechanism
the client-facing axes on which the routes genuinely differ
the rule that the route is explained before any plan name enters the conversation
excluded: ranking the routes or naming a winner
specific premiums, cost-sharing amounts or benefit values
carrier-specific plan design detail, which belongs to the per-plan verification and comparison work

pros.claim: A client who understands the mechanism can evaluate any plan they later encounter, including ones the agent does not offer
pros.example: a client who grasps network-versus-program access correctly interpreting a mailer from a carrier the agent has no appointment with

pros.claim: Explaining routes before names prevents brand anchoring and makes the later comparison feel like a choice rather than a pitch
pros.example: a client who arrived asking for a specific advertised plan first learning what class it belongs to and what that class trades away

cons.claim: Mechanism explanation takes time and some clients want a name immediately
cons.example: a client saying repeatedly that their neighbour has a plan they want and resisting the structural explanation

cons.claim: Simplifying two complex architectures into contrasting axes always loses detail that matters to somebody
cons.example: a portability contrast that understates how one route's emergency and travel provisions actually behave for a specific client's situation

failure_modes: presenting one route as generally better rather than differently shaped
naming plans before the client understands the class they belong to
describing extra bundled benefits as the deciding factor when access and drug fit dominate for this client
using carrier marketing language instead of mechanism language
acceptance_tests: the file shows the route mechanisms were explained before any plan name, with the axes used recorded
no statement in the comparison ranks a route as better in general rather than better on a stated client criterion
revisit_triggers: a structural change in how a route works for the plan year
the client's priorities shift between predictability, access and cost
a client demonstrates they have misunderstood how one route pays

base.update_signal: a structural change in how either route pays, grants access or bundles drug coverage for the plan year

nodes.definition: Make explicit the asymmetry that makes route choice consequential rather than merely comparative: supplement policies are generally issued without health questions only during limited guaranteed-acceptance window classes tied to first eligibility or to specific triggering situations, and outside those, carriers in most states may apply medical underwriting, so a client who leaves the supplement route may not be able to return on the same terms if their health has changed. State variation here is large - some states impose far more generous rules, and a few operate quite different regimes - and carrier practice varies within a state. The agent's obligation is therefore threefold: flag the asymmetry plainly as the part of the decision that is hardest to undo, decline to promise that a future switch back will be available, and verify the client's own state's current rules and the specific carriers' underwriting practice before the client relies on reversibility. This is the single point where an otherwise reasonable cost comparison can quietly become an irreversible decision.

included: the guaranteed-acceptance window classes and the underwriting exposure outside them
the state-variation and carrier-practice warning and the duty to verify both
the written asymmetry statement given before an election that leaves the supplement route
excluded: predicting whether a specific client would pass underwriting, which only the carrier decides
quoting state rules as settled fact rather than verifying them for the client's state and plan year
medical assessment of the client's health trajectory

pros.claim: Naming the one-way door converts a cost decision into an informed risk decision the client actually owns
pros.example: a healthy client choosing lower fixed cost while acknowledging in writing that returning later may require answering health questions

pros.claim: Verifying state rules prevents applying a rule of thumb from another state to a client it does not govern
pros.example: an agent licensed in two states checking each client's own state rather than assuming the more generous regime applies

cons.claim: The warning can frighten clients away from a route that would genuinely suit them
cons.example: a client with tight cash flow rejecting a suitable lower-premium option purely on the reversibility warning

cons.claim: The rules are state-specific and change, so the agent carries a standing verification burden that is easy to let slide
cons.example: relying on a two-year-old understanding of a state's rules during a busy season

failure_modes: telling a client they can always switch back
applying one state's rules to a client in another
burying the asymmetry in a document instead of saying it out loud
treating a guaranteed-acceptance trigger as available without verifying the client's situation actually triggers it
acceptance_tests: any election that leaves or forgoes the supplement route carries a dated written statement of the underwriting asymmetry, acknowledged by the client
the state rules and carrier underwriting practice relied on are cited with the source and date checked, for the client's own state
revisit_triggers: the client's state changes its supplement issue rules
a carrier changes its underwriting practice or guaranteed-issue triggers
the client moves to another state

base.update_signal: a change in the client's state's supplement issue rules or in a carrier's underwriting practice

nodes.definition: Build the cost picture as a structure with four parts rather than as a single number: the fixed monthly cost the client pays whatever happens, which includes plan premium plus any program premium they pay directly plus a supplement premium where that route applies; the expected cost-sharing implied by the utilization the client themselves described; the drug cost across the year's phases from the fit analysis; and the worst-case ceiling, meaning the annual out-of-pocket maximum where the architecture has one and the explicit absence of such a ceiling where it does not. Every figure entering the model comes from a current-year official source for that specific plan and is dated in the file. The model is presented as a range with its assumptions visible, and the agent states which single assumption most changes the answer - usually hospital or specialty-drug utilization - so the client can judge how fragile the comparison is. The purpose is to kill the lowest-premium-wins reflex without replacing it with false precision the agent cannot defend.

included: the four-part cost structure and the ranges built from it
sourcing and dating every figure to a current-year official lookup for that plan
naming the assumption that most moves the result and showing the worst-case ceiling or its absence
excluded: predicting the client's actual utilization or health events
quoting premiums, cost-sharing or ceilings as remembered facts rather than dated lookups
financial planning, tax treatment or budgeting advice for the household

pros.claim: Showing worst case next to monthly cost reframes the decision as risk tolerance rather than price shopping
pros.example: a client who had fixed on the lowest premium reconsidering once the presence or absence of an annual ceiling is on the same page

pros.claim: Ranges with visible assumptions survive scrutiny where a single confident number does not
pros.example: a client returning in March with unexpected costs and finding the file already showed that outcome inside the stated range

cons.claim: Ranges are harder for clients to compare than one number, and some will simply pick the smallest figure they see
cons.example: a client reading only the low end of two ranges and treating the difference as the answer

cons.claim: The model rests on self-reported utilization that clients estimate badly in both directions
cons.example: a client who says they never go to hospital having two admissions in the coverage year

failure_modes: comparing premiums only and calling it a cost comparison
using a prior plan year's figures because the current ones were not yet published when the conversation started
presenting a point estimate that implies precision the inputs do not support
omitting the program premium the client pays directly, which distorts the comparison between routes
acceptance_tests: each option in the comparison shows fixed cost, expected cost-sharing, drug cost and worst-case ceiling or its explicit absence
every figure cites the plan-year source and the date it was looked up, and the assumption with the largest effect is named in writing
revisit_triggers: the plan year's published figures change after the model was built
the client revises their expected utilization or a new diagnosis changes it
actual costs after the effective date fall outside the stated range

base.update_signal: published plan-year figures change, or observed client costs land consistently outside the modelled ranges

nodes.definition: Install an explicit control against the one bias this business structurally carries: compensation differs between product classes and between a first-time enrollment and a switch, so the agent's interest and the client's can diverge without anyone intending it. The control has parts that must all be present. The client's criteria and must-keep constraints are fixed in writing before any candidate set is assembled, so the criteria cannot be reverse-engineered from the preferred product. The comparison must include at least one option that pays the agent less or nothing at all, including the do-nothing baseline. The written rationale for each shown option is expressed in the client's own recorded criteria rather than in product language. The limited-carrier disclosure is stated plainly so the client knows the set is bounded. And periodically the agent inspects their own book for a skew toward one product class that the client mix does not explain, treating an unexplained skew as a finding to investigate rather than a result to enjoy. Compensation itself is set by regulated schedules and is described here only as a mechanism whose current plan-year rules must be verified - never as an input to a plan choice.

included: criteria-before-candidates sequencing and the written rationale in client language
the requirement that lower-paying and do-nothing options appear in the set
the periodic book-skew self-audit and what to do when skew is unexplained
excluded: compensation amounts, schedules and renewal mechanics, which the renewal-compensation KB owns and which are regulated and verified per plan year
carrier contracting and appointment economics
any use of compensation as a comparison criterion, which is prohibited outright

pros.claim: Fixing criteria before candidates makes steering detectable by a third party reading the file
pros.example: a reviewer able to see that the must-keep list predates the shortlist and that the recommended option maps to it line by line

pros.claim: A book-skew audit catches drift that no single case review would ever reveal
pros.example: noticing that nearly every enrollment in a season landed in one product class while the client mix was unchanged, and auditing recent comparisons for why

cons.claim: Skew can be innocent, so the audit produces false alarms that cost time to clear
cons.example: a genuine local shift in plan quality producing a concentration that looks like steering and is not

cons.claim: The control constrains the agent's freedom to lead with what they know best, which can slow good conversations
cons.example: having to build out an unfamiliar option because the client's criteria point at it

failure_modes: assembling candidates first and writing the criteria afterwards to fit
quietly excluding the do-nothing option because it earns nothing
letting product-class familiarity substitute for a client-criteria rationale
explaining away an unexplained book skew instead of auditing it
acceptance_tests: the recorded criteria and must-keep list are dated before the candidate set, and each shown option has a rationale expressed in those criteria
the comparison contains the do-nothing baseline and at least one option that does not maximise the agent's compensation
a book-level review of product-class distribution exists for the period, with any unexplained skew recorded and investigated
revisit_triggers: compensation structures change for the plan year
the book shows a product-class skew the client mix does not explain
a client or reviewer questions why a particular option was or was not shown

base.update_signal: a change in compensation structure for the plan year, or a book-skew audit that finds an unexplained concentration

nodes.definition: Assemble the small set of options actually shown to the client and the written reason those and not others. The assembly rules are strict because this is where integrity is either preserved or lost. Every option must satisfy the recorded must-keep provider and drug constraints, or be shown explicitly as failing them with the failure named rather than the option silently dropped. The client's current arrangement stays in the set as the do-nothing baseline so that changing has to earn its place. Where the agent's carrier access cannot satisfy a stated need, that gap is named out loud and the client is pointed to the official comparison tool or the neutral counseling programme rather than being talked out of the need. The set is kept small enough to be understood - a handful of options on a single comparison sheet the client keeps - with the same fields shown for each so nothing is hidden by omission, and each option's rationale is written in the client's own criteria.

included: the assembly rules, including constraint-failure visibility and the do-nothing baseline
the named-gap rule and the outward referral when carrier access cannot meet a need
the one-sheet comparison with identical fields per option and per-option rationale
excluded: making the choice for the client
showing plans the agent is not appointed to transact as if they were available through them
compensation as a comparison field or a selection reason

pros.claim: Showing constraint failures rather than hiding them keeps the client's stated needs sovereign over the agent's inventory
pros.example: leaving a low-cost plan on the sheet marked as excluding the client's cardiologist, so the client sees the trade rather than never meeting it

pros.claim: Naming a gap the agent cannot fill builds the credibility that drives referrals more reliably than winning the case would
pros.example: telling a client that none of the available options keeps their surgeon in network and pointing them to the official tool and counseling programme

cons.claim: A set that includes failing options and a do-nothing baseline is more confusing than a curated recommendation
cons.example: a client fixating on the cheapest sheet row that is marked as failing a must-keep constraint

cons.claim: Naming gaps sends business away and the discipline erodes fastest in a thin season
cons.example: an agent quietly reframing a must-keep provider as nice-to-keep when no available plan includes them

failure_modes: silently dropping options that fail a constraint so the trade-off is never seen
omitting the do-nothing baseline
showing different fields for different options so one looks better by omission
relaxing a must-keep constraint without the client explicitly changing it in writing
acceptance_tests: the comparison sheet shows the same fields for every option, includes the do-nothing baseline, and marks any must-keep constraint failure explicitly
each option carries a written rationale in the client's recorded criteria, and any need the agent's access cannot meet is named with the outward referral recorded
revisit_triggers: a must-keep constraint changes or the client revises their criteria
verification invalidates an option after the sheet was built
the agent's carrier access changes what can be shown

base.update_signal: a constraint failure or a carrier-access change that invalidates an option after the sheet was assembled

nodes.definition: Run the meeting itself in an order that keeps the beneficiary in control from the first minute to the election. Restate the agreed scope and the limited-carrier disclosure; confirm the intake facts out loud and correct them; explain the route mechanism before any plan name is spoken; walk the comparison sheet field by field on the client's own criteria, stating each trade-off in both directions including what the option costs them and not only what it gives; check comprehension by asking the client to state the central trade-off back in their own words; answer the inevitable request for a personal recommendation by returning to their recorded criteria rather than issuing a directive; and offer time to think as the default rather than as a concession extracted by a hesitant client. The agent's own pipeline pressure never enters the room. The only deadlines mentioned are the client's real window dates, stated with their source, and if the client wants to end the meeting undecided that is recorded as a normal outcome rather than treated as a failure to be salvaged.

included: the meeting order from scope restatement through election
the two-sided trade-off presentation and the restate-it-back comprehension check
the answer pattern for 'which would you choose' and the default offer of time
excluded: the regulatory text of disclosures and recording requirements, owned by the certifications-and-marketing KB
making the election on the client's behalf
post-submission verification, which follows this step

pros.claim: A fixed order stops the meeting from collapsing into the client's first question and leaving the trade-offs unspoken
pros.example: a client who opens with 'my friend has this plan' still hearing route mechanism and constraint checks before that plan is discussed

pros.claim: Two-sided trade-off statements protect the client from the pleasant version of the truth
pros.example: saying plainly that a lower premium option adds referral steps and prior-authorization paperwork the client will personally have to manage

cons.claim: The full order takes longer than most clients expect and longer than peak-season slots allow
cons.example: a scheduled hour running past ninety minutes because the comprehension check revealed a misunderstanding worth fixing

cons.claim: Refusing to recommend frustrates clients who want to be told, and some read it as evasiveness
cons.example: a client who asks four times which plan the agent's own parent would take

failure_modes: presenting benefits without the corresponding costs
letting the client elect immediately after hearing only their preferred option
answering the recommendation question with a directive because the client insisted
mentioning a deadline the agent cannot source to the client's real window
acceptance_tests: the file records the meeting order followed, that trade-offs were stated in both directions, and the client's restatement of the central trade-off
the election, if taken, is recorded as the client's own and no undecided outcome was pressured toward a signature
revisit_triggers: a comprehension check fails or the client's account of the decision later differs from the file
the comparison changes materially between meetings
a complaint or review names the conduct of the meeting

base.update_signal: post-enrollment complaints or comprehension failures that trace to how the meeting was conducted

nodes.definition: Submit the election the client actually made, correctly, on the first attempt. That means selecting the enrollment-period code matching the window the client genuinely qualifies for and recording the evidence of qualification alongside it; entering names, identifiers and dates exactly as they appear on the client's own program card rather than as the client spells them; completing every required attestation and consent artifact including the recorded-consent classes that apply when the sale happens by telephone or electronic method; confirming the effective date the submission will produce and saying it back to the client in the same sentence as what they must not do before then; and capturing the confirmation identifier in the file immediately. Wrong window codes and mismatched identifiers are the two errors that most reliably turn a completed conversation into a rejected application and a client without coverage on the date they were expecting - and often the window has closed by the time the rejection surfaces.

included: window-code selection with recorded qualifying evidence
identifier and date accuracy taken from the client's own card
required attestations and consent artifacts, effective-date confirmation and confirmation-identifier capture
excluded: choosing the plan, which is the client's decision
the regulatory specification of consent and recording rules, owned by the certifications-and-marketing KB
carrier-side processing and underwriting decisions

pros.claim: Getting the window code and identifiers right the first time is the difference between coverage on the expected date and a gap the client cannot fix
pros.example: an application accepted cleanly because the qualifying-event evidence was attached with the code rather than requested weeks later

pros.claim: Saying the effective date back to the client prevents the most common post-sale surprise
pros.example: a client told plainly that their current plan continues until a stated date and that they should not cancel anything before it

cons.claim: Careful submission takes meeting time at the exact moment both parties feel finished
cons.example: twenty extra minutes at the end of a long appointment checking a card digit by digit while the client is tired

cons.claim: Submission mechanics differ by carrier and by channel, so a routine that works in one place fails in another
cons.example: an electronic signature flow accepted by one carrier and rejected as incomplete by another

failure_modes: choosing a window code that is convenient rather than the one the client qualifies for
typing identifiers from memory or from a prior form instead of the client's card
skipping a required consent artifact on a phone or electronic sale
leaving the meeting without the confirmation identifier recorded
acceptance_tests: the submitted window code matches the window class in the file and its qualifying evidence is attached
identifiers and dates were verified against the client's own program card, all required consent artifacts exist, and the confirmation identifier and effective date are recorded in the file
revisit_triggers: the carrier or program rejects or queries the application
the client's window or qualifying evidence changes before processing completes
the carrier changes its submission or consent requirements

base.update_signal: a carrier or program change to submission, window-code or consent requirements, or a run of rejected applications with a common cause

nodes.definition: Treat submission as the middle of the job, not the end, and close the gap between an application sent and a person actually covered. Verify acceptance and the effective date through the carrier's own channel rather than assuming silence means success; confirm the client received their cards and welcome materials and knows what to carry; check that the prior arrangement ended or continued exactly as intended, including whether the new election automatically disenrolled a previous plan and whether anything the client was told to keep is still in force; where drug coverage changed, verify a first fill at the client's own pharmacy so a formulary restriction or pharmacy-network surprise surfaces while it can still be worked; and correct errors while the correction window is still open, which is a far narrower opportunity than clients assume. Anything unresolved is escalated through the carrier's or program's defined process, and the client is told plainly what was escalated, to whom, and when an answer is expected.

included: acceptance and effective-date confirmation through the carrier channel
card, prior-coverage and first-fill checks
error correction inside the available window and escalation through the defined process
excluded: ongoing year-round service, mid-year plan changes and annual review, owned by the renewal-service KB
acting as the client's legal representative in an appeal
claims adjudication

pros.claim: A first-fill check turns a formulary restriction from a January crisis into a December task
pros.example: discovering at the pharmacy counter test that a maintenance drug needs prior authorization, and getting the prescriber engaged before coverage starts

pros.claim: Confirming what the election disenrolled prevents the double-coverage and no-coverage surprises that destroy trust
pros.example: verifying that a previous plan ended on the intended date rather than leaving the client paying two premiums

cons.claim: This work lands in the busiest weeks and earns nothing directly, so it is the first thing dropped under load
cons.example: verification calls deferred through the peak and never made for a batch of December enrollments

cons.claim: Carrier confirmation channels are slow and inconsistent, so verification can take several attempts per case
cons.example: an acceptance that cannot be confirmed until after the client's cards arrive anyway

failure_modes: assuming acceptance because nothing was heard back
never checking whether the prior plan actually ended
skipping the first-fill check for clients whose drug coverage changed
discovering an error after the correction window has closed
acceptance_tests: acceptance, effective date, card receipt and prior-coverage status are each confirmed and dated in the file
for every client whose drug coverage changed, a first-fill outcome is recorded, and any unresolved item shows the escalation path, the date raised and the expected answer date
revisit_triggers: the carrier reports a discrepancy or the client reports not receiving cards
a first fill is refused or costs materially more than modelled
the client says their previous coverage is still billing them

base.update_signal: a pattern of post-effective problems that the current verification steps did not catch

nodes.definition: Produce and retain the file that would let someone with no memory of the meeting reconstruct why this client ended up with this coverage.
